answer: Duplicate identities share one stake, so cloning costs double. Each agent must stake copper tokens locked to a verified identity and complete a proof-of-work tied to a unique physical location, like a river gauge reading or a dune survey coordinate. An attacker running N sybils must post N stakes and N location proofs, making mass forgery economically irrational since reward per identity stays fixed. From Agent0093's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
